fit: limited dark chocolate within Mediterranean advice and Parkinson anxiety
assessment: The protocol restricts dark chocolate to at most one weekly serving. The trial assigns counseling plus standard care and reports HAM-A group-by-week p=.745. It cannot estimate a culinary dark-chocolate effect.

fit: generic cooking and dressing oil within dietary program and Parkinson anxiety
assessment: The intervention assigns a complete Mediterranean diet plus standard care, without oil grade or a separate oil dose. The anxiety interaction is p=.745 and the supplement records nutrient totals only.

fit: unprepared orange intake frequency and categorical Bristol stool form
assessment: The 100-person adult cross-sectional survey gives Pearson chi-square 56.548 on 35 df (p=.012). The cells and direction are unavailable. Parkinson disease and constipation severity were outside the study design.

fit: orange frequency and Bristol stool form in university students
assessment: The separate reported sample of 1,144 students gives orange p=.001 without a directional cross-tab. It excluded diagnosed constipation and diarrhea. Orange preparation and Parkinson constipation severity were outside the study design.

fit: blended orange and other fruits with physical therapy in Chagas megacolon
assessment: Constipation scores fell in 11 of 12 participants after six weeks (paired p<.0022). Four reported bloating or flatulence with the drink. The study groups multiple ingredients with physical therapy and has no control or Parkinson population. The 2010 thesis abstract describes the same cohort.

fit: pasteurized orange juice products and stool frequency in healthy adults
assessment: Forty-eight adults consumed regular or levan-enriched lower-sugar orange juice. Table 3 reports p=.02 for time and p=.79 for product by time. Both arms received juice. This does not estimate the effect of raw whole oranges on Parkinson constipation.

fit: initial encounter constipation records and medicinal citrus prescriptions
assessment: The hospital study reports constipation in 1,022 of 3,206 initial encounters and counts Citrus aurantium entries in mixed decoctions. Records give prescription and symptom frequencies without measured citrus consumption or a constipation change.
